tests/test_aerofs_studio_api.py.file_doc:
Unit & Integration Tests for AeroFS Studio API Additions
Tests health endpoint, file listing, snapshot listing, file duplicate (CAS dedup),
benchmark suite, and CORS headers.

tests.name: test_file_deletion_and_reoccupation
tests.doc:
Tests that when files are deleted, their blocks are freed,
and new files created afterwards reclaim and occupy that space efficiently via Best-Fit.

tests.name: test_large_file_skips_small_hole_in_contiguous_mode_and_fills_in_hole_filling_mode
tests.doc:
Directly validates the user scenario:
- Free Hole 1 has 8 blocks (sectors 4..11).
- File 1 needs 64 blocks.
- Contiguous Best-Fit skips Hole 1 because 8 < 64 (avoiding fragmentation),
  allocating the 64 blocks contiguously in Hole 2 (sectors 14..77).
- An 8-block file fits Hole 1 exactly (sectors 4..11).
- In fill_holes_first=True mode, the 64-block file fills Hole 1 first (4..11)
  and spills remainder into Hole 2.

tests/test_comprehensive_validation.py.file_doc:
AeroFS Comprehensive Validation Suite
======================================
Validates every subsystem according to the AeroFS Test Suite and Recovery
Validation Plan. This single file covers Sections 3–6 and 8 of the plan:

  Section 3 — Core Storage (block device, dedup, CoW/snapshots)
  Section 4 — Verified Self-Healing (A through F, highest priority)
  Section 5 — API & Client end-to-end integration
  Section 6 — Persistence and restart (documents limitations honestly)
  Section 8 — Benchmark measurements with honest simulated-value labelling

Design principles:
  - Deterministic known byte patterns for all test data.
  - Pre-corruption reference values (hashes, roots, bytes) are always captured
    BEFORE any corruption is injected — never re-derived from corrupt bytes.
  - Exact byte-for-byte comparisons after every recovery.
  - Negative / boundary / regression tests alongside positive paths.
  - Each test creates its own disposable disk and cleans up on failure.
  - Tests are order-independent (no shared state between tests).

tests.name: test_superblock_magic_and_reserved_blocks
tests.doc: Superblock magic is valid and blocks 0-3 are reserved/allocated.

tests.name: test_write_read_exact_bytes
tests.doc: Allocated block write/read returns exact bytes with no corruption.

tests.name: test_write_smaller_than_block_is_padded
tests.doc: Data smaller than block size is zero-padded on write.

tests.name: test_reject_data_larger_than_block
tests.doc: Writing data larger than block size raises ValueError.

tests.name: test_reject_invalid_block_id_read
tests.doc: Reading an out-of-bounds block ID raises IndexError.

tests.name: test_reject_invalid_block_id_write
tests.doc: Writing to an out-of-bounds block ID raises IndexError.

tests.name: test_free_block_zeroes_content_and_bitmap
tests.doc: free_block() zeroes content on disk and clears the bitmap entry.

tests.name: test_allocation_stats_decrease_on_free
tests.doc: Allocation stats reflect freed block correctly.

tests.name: test_allocation_exhaustion
tests.doc: Allocating all blocks raises OSError without corrupting existing data.

tests.name: test_disk_reopen_preserves_allocation_bitmap
tests.doc: Re-opening an existing disk re-loads the allocation bitmap correctly.

tests.name: test_block_boundaries_exact_and_one_off
tests.doc: Validate behavior with exact block size, one byte below, and one byte above.

tests.name: test_inject_bit_rot_only_on_allocated_block
tests.doc: inject_bit_rot raises ValueError for unallocated blocks.

tests.name: test_identical_files_share_physical_blocks
tests.doc: Two files with identical content share exact physical block IDs.

tests.name: test_reference_counts_increment_on_dedup
tests.doc: Deduplication increments reference counts on shared blocks.

tests.name: test_delete_one_of_two_sharing_files_leaves_other_readable
tests.doc: Deleting one file that shares blocks leaves the other file fully readable.

tests.name: test_reference_count_drops_to_zero_on_full_delete
tests.doc: After deleting all files sharing a block, its refcount reaches 0 and block is freed.

tests.name: test_partially_identical_files_only_dedup_matching_chunks
tests.doc: Only identical 4 KB chunks are deduplicated; different chunks allocate new blocks.

tests.name: test_empty_file_write_and_read
tests.doc: Empty file can be written and read back as empty bytes.

tests.name: test_exact_block_size_file
tests.doc: A file of exactly one block size allocates exactly one block.

tests.name: test_one_byte_below_block_boundary
tests.doc: File one byte short of block boundary allocates exactly one block.

tests.name: test_one_byte_above_block_boundary
tests.doc: File one byte over block boundary allocates exactly two blocks.

tests.name: test_multi_block_file_content_integrity
tests.doc: Multi-block file reads back correct content for each chunk.

tests.name: test_replace_file_clears_stale_hash_index
tests.doc: Overwriting a file with different content removes stale hash-to-block mappings.

tests.name: test_dedup_never_returns_block_with_wrong_hash
tests.doc: The dedup engine never returns a block whose actual bytes differ from expected hash.

tests.name: test_snapshot_preserves_original_after_file_modification
tests.doc: After modifying a live file, snapshot retains original exact bytes.

tests.name: test_snapshot_preserves_original_after_file_deletion
tests.doc: Deleting a live file does not destroy its data in a prior snapshot.

tests.name: test_snapshot_restore_returns_all_filenames
tests.doc: Restored snapshot reinstates all filenames that existed at snap time.

tests.name: test_duplicate_snapshot_name_raises
tests.doc: Creating a snapshot with an already-existing name raises ValueError.

tests.name: test_restore_nonexistent_snapshot_raises
tests.doc: Restoring a non-existent snapshot raises KeyError.

tests.name: test_snapshot_does_not_increase_physical_block_count
tests.doc: Creating a snapshot does not allocate additional data blocks.

tests.name: test_snapshot_reference_counts_are_incremented
tests.doc: Snapshot increments reference counts so shared blocks are not freed on file delete.

tests.name: test_delete_snapshot_releases_unreferenced_blocks
tests.doc: Deleting a snapshot releases blocks that are no longer referenced.

tests.name: test_repeated_restore_produces_consistent_state
tests.doc: Restoring the same snapshot multiple times yields identical state each time.

tests.name: test_fresh_filesystem_scrub_is_healthy
tests.doc: A freshly written filesystem always scrubs as HEALTHY with zero corrupted blocks.

tests.name: test_scrub_returns_correct_file_count
tests.doc: scrub_all() reports exactly the number of active files.

tests.name: test_leaf_hashes_match_actual_disk_bytes_on_write
tests.doc:
After write_file(), every stored leaf hash must match the actual bytes
physically on disk — pre-corruption baseline integrity check.

tests.name: test_merkle_root_matches_tree_recompute
tests.doc:
The inode's stored merkle_root matches what a freshly-built MerkleTree
computes from the same blocks.

tests.name: test_bit_rot_changes_disk_bytes
tests.doc: inject_bit_rot() verifiably changes the physical bytes on disk.

tests.name: test_scrub_detects_corrupted_block_using_pre_corruption_hashes
tests.doc:
Critical: The audit uses leaf_hashes recorded BEFORE corruption.
It must report exactly the corrupted block ID.

tests.name: test_clean_block_not_reported_as_corrupted
tests.doc: A block whose bytes have not changed must not appear in corrupted list.

tests.name: test_multi_block_multi_file_corruption_all_detected
tests.doc: Corruption in several blocks across several files is all detected.

tests.name: test_shared_deduplicated_block_corruption_detected
tests.doc:
Corruption of a deduplicated block shared by two files is detected
for both files in the scrub report.

tests.name: test_unallocated_block_corruption_handled_safely
tests.doc: Injecting bit-rot on an unallocated block raises ValueError safely.

tests.name: test_scrub_never_rebuilds_expected_hash_from_corrupt_bytes
tests.doc:
The scrub comparison is always against the pre-recorded leaf_hashes
on the inode, NOT recomputed from possibly-corrupt disk bytes.

Verified by: corrupting a block, then confirming the scrub reports
DEGRADED using the stored (pre-corruption) leaf_hashes as the reference.

tests.name: test_recovery_cache_populated_at_write_time
tests.doc: write_file() populates recovery_cache with the exact block bytes.

tests.name: test_tier1_heals_exact_bytes_from_cache
tests.doc:
After heal, the block's bytes are byte-for-byte identical to the
known-good original preserved in recovery_cache.

tests.name: test_tier1_heal_passes_trusted_hash_check
tests.doc: Recovered block hash matches the trusted pre-corruption leaf hash.

tests.name: test_tier1_does_not_corrupt_unrelated_blocks
tests.doc: Healing one block does not alter the bytes of any other block.

tests.name: test_tier1_heal_log_records_block_source_and_hashes
tests.doc: HealRecord in heal_log contains block_id, source, hashes, and success.

tests.name: test_tier1_dedup_index_consistent_after_heal
tests.doc:
After healing, the block-to-hash mapping in the dedup engine still
matches the repaired bytes on disk.

tests.name: test_tier1_post_heal_scrub_is_healthy
tests.doc: After successful Tier-1 heal, a new scrub reports HEALTHY.

tests.name: test_tier1_full_file_readable_after_heal
tests.doc: Full file content reads back correctly after multi-block Tier-1 heal.

tests.name: test_tier2_snapshot_path_is_tried_when_cache_cleared
tests.doc:
When recovery_cache entry is explicitly removed, the code must attempt
the snapshot extent search path (Tier 2). This is confirmed via heal_record.

tests.name: test_snapshot_remains_unchanged_after_heal
tests.doc: The snapshot's inode state is unaffected by the healing operation.

tests.name: test_merkle_leaf_hashes_updated_only_after_successful_restore
tests.doc:
Merkle leaf hashes are re-anchored on the inode ONLY after successful
recovery — not before, and not in failed cases.
Verified by checking the post-heal leaf hash matches actual disk bytes.

tests.name: test_full_scrub_healthy_after_tier2_snap_heal
tests.doc:
End-to-end: write → snap → evict cache → corrupt → heal (Tier-2 path)
→ post-heal scrub HEALTHY.

tests.name: test_unrecoverable_block_not_reported_as_healed
tests.doc: A block with no valid recovery source is marked unrecoverable, not healed.

tests.name: test_unrecoverable_does_not_update_leaf_hash_to_corrupt_value
tests.doc:
Critical safety: A failed heal must never re-anchor the inode's
leaf_hash or merkle_root to hashes of the corrupted bytes.

tests.name: test_failed_recovery_does_not_corrupt_unrelated_files
tests.doc: A failed heal operation leaves unrelated files untouched.

tests.name: test_audit_log_distinguishes_healed_from_unrecoverable
tests.doc:
Audit log entries clearly distinguish: healed (success=True) vs.
unrecoverable (success=False, source='failed').

tests.name: test_repeated_healing_is_idempotent
tests.doc: Running self_heal_all() multiple times on the same state is safe and correct.

tests.name: test_repeated_scrubbing_is_idempotent
tests.doc: Multiple scrub calls on a healthy filesystem always return HEALTHY.

tests.name: test_shared_block_corruption_reported_for_both_owners
tests.doc:
A corrupt deduplicated block shared by two files is reported as
corrupted in both files' scrub detail entries.

tests.name: test_proof_for_one_block_file
tests.doc: Single-block file proof is valid and references the correct block.

tests.name: test_proof_for_even_sized_multi_block_file
tests.doc: Even number of blocks produces valid proof for each leaf.

tests.name: test_proof_for_odd_sized_multi_block_file
tests.doc: Odd number of blocks produces valid proof for each leaf (last node is duplicated).

tests.name: test_proof_rejects_invalid_leaf_index
tests.doc: Out-of-range leaf index returns valid=False or raises IndexError.

tests.name: test_proof_leaf_hash_matches_actual_block
tests.doc: Proof leaf_hash matches the actual SHA-256 of the block on disk.

tests.name: test_proof_root_matches_stored_merkle_root
tests.doc: Proof root_hash matches the inode's stored merkle_root.

tests.name: test_new_tree_after_heal_built_from_repaired_bytes
tests.doc:
Post-heal MerkleTree root is computed from the repaired bytes,
NOT from the corrupted bytes. Verified by re-building the tree
independently and comparing.

tests.name: test_post_heal_scrub_is_healthy_for_recoverable_case
tests.doc: After successful heal, post-heal scrub is HEALTHY with zero corrupted blocks.

tests.name: test_telemetry_endpoint_structure
tests.doc: GET /api/telemetry returns required fields.

tests.name: test_file_create_read_delete_lifecycle
tests.doc: Full file lifecycle: create, read, delete via REST API.

tests.name: test_snapshot_create_list_restore_delete
tests.doc: Snapshot lifecycle: create, list, restore, delete.

tests.name: test_bitrot_inject_scrub_heal_endpoint_cycle
tests.doc: Full bit-rot cycle via REST: inject → scrub (DEGRADED) → heal → scrub (HEALTHY).

tests.name: test_block_inspect_returns_telemetry
tests.doc: GET /api/blocks/{id} returns block telemetry for valid allocated blocks.

tests.name: test_merkle_proof_endpoint
tests.doc: GET /api/merkle/proof/{filename}/{block_index} returns valid proof.

tests.name: test_heal_log_endpoint
tests.doc: GET /api/merkle/heal_log returns a list of heal events.

tests.name: test_client_server_failure_raises_not_hides_error
tests.doc: Client to a bad URL raises an exception, not a misleading success.

tests.class_doc:
Documents the persistence guarantees (and limitations) of AeroFS.

AeroFS persistence model:
─ Physical block data: PERSISTED on disk (binary container file)
─ Allocation bitmap:   PERSISTED on disk (written to block 1 after each alloc/free)
─ Superblock:          PERSISTED on disk (block 0)
─ File metadata (inodes, filenames, block_ids, leaf_hashes, merkle_root):
                       MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted; lost on process restart
─ Dedup hash-to-block index: MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted
─ Reference counts:    MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted
─ Snapshots:           MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted
─ Recovery cache:      MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted
─ Heal log:            MEMORY-ONLY — not persisted

Tests below verify what IS persisted and explicitly mark what is NOT.
tests.name: test_block_data_persists_across_reopen
tests.doc: Physical block bytes are present after closing and reopening the disk.

tests/test_crash_recovery.py.file_doc:
Comprehensive Crash Resilience & Metadata Recovery Test Suite for AeroFS
========================================================================
Validates filesystem durability under simulated crashes, power failures,
torn writes, and unhandled process terminations.

tests.name: test_crash_clean_restart_recovery
tests.doc:
Scenario 1: Normal crash / sudden process exit between operations.
Verifies that all committed state (inodes, CAS dedup tables, snapshots,
block mappings, and Merkle roots) survives process termination and is
faithfully reconstructed on mount.

tests.name: test_crash_mid_journal_write_atomic_rename
tests.doc:
Scenario 2: Crash occurs MID-WRITE while saving metadata.
MetadataJournal writes to a temporary file (.tmp) first and uses atomic
POSIX os.replace() to commit. If a crash leaves a half-written or corrupted
.tmp file, the primary journal remains intact and uncorrupted.

tests.name: test_crash_corrupted_journal_graceful_fallback
tests.doc:
Scenario 3: Physical media sector corruption damages the journal itself.
If the journal JSON file is corrupted or unreadable, AeroFS must not crash
with an unhandled exception. It should log a warning and fall back safely.

tests.name: test_crash_recovery_cache_tier1_heals_after_restart
tests.doc:
Scenario 4: Recovery cache persistence across crashes.
A block written in process 1 is corrupted AFTER process 2 mounts the disk.
Process 2 must be able to restore the block using the persisted Tier-1
recovery cache saved by Process 1.

tests.name: test_crash_extent_store_tier2_heals_after_restart
tests.doc:
Scenario 5: Snapshot extent store persistence across crashes.
A snapshot taken in process 1 is persisted. After process 2 mounts,
the live block is corrupted and recovery cache is evicted.
Process 2 must successfully heal from the historical snapshot extent store.

tests.name: test_crash_copy_on_write_atomicity_preserves_old_version
tests.doc:
Scenario 6: Copy-on-Write write atomicity.
When a file is modified, CoW allocates new blocks. The old block is never
overwritten in-place. If a crash occurs before the file's inode pointer
is updated, the historical snapshot still points to the uncorrupted old block.

tests/test_risk_mitigations.py.file_doc:
Tests for AeroFS Remaining Risk Mitigations (Risks 1 to 8)
==========================================================
Verifies that all 8 architectural enhancements and edge-case mitigations
identified in the AeroFS Validation Report are functional, robust, and tested.

tests.name: test_risk1_tier2_independent_snapshot_extent_store
tests.doc:
Risk 1 Mitigation:
Snapshot extent store captures an independent byte copy at snapshot time.
When live physical block is corrupted and recovery_cache is cleared, Tier-2
heals the block from the snapshot extent store rather than failing on
the corrupted live block.

tests.name: test_risk2_and_3_metadata_and_cache_persistence
tests.doc:
Risks 2 & 3 Mitigation:
MetadataJournal persists file inodes, CAS dedup tables, snapshots,
snapshot extent stores, and recovery cache.

tests.name: test_risk4_measured_os_baseline_benchmark
tests.doc:
Risk 4 Mitigation:
benchmark.py uses a measured file copy against the OS filesystem instead of
a fixed hardcoded simulated constant.

tests.name: test_risk5_bit_rot_random_positions
tests.doc:
Risk 5 Mitigation:
inject_bit_rot() flips bytes randomly across the entire 4 KB block
instead of only touching the first 16 bytes.

tests.name: test_risk6_server_test_reset_endpoint
tests.doc:
Risk 6 Mitigation:
FastAPI app provides /api/test/reset and /api/format with clean state
re-initialization.

tests.name: test_risk7_operation_timeouts
tests.doc:
Risk 7 Mitigation:
write_file_with_timeout() and scrub_with_timeout() enforce wall-clock limits
to guard against runaway checks or hanging virtual storage devices.

tests.name: test_risk8_merkle_tree_caching
tests.doc:
Risk 8 Mitigation:
get_cached_merkle_tree() caches the computed MerkleTree structure by root hash,
avoiding redundant disk reads on repeated inspect or proof queries.
Cache is updated with new tree on write and evicted on file deletion.

tests/test_self_healing.py.file_doc:
Verified Self-Healing Test Suite for AeroFS
============================================
Tests the strengthened Merkle scrubbing and autonomous self-healing engine.

Coverage:
  1. scrub_all_files() — aggregated report structure
  2. Merkle inclusion proof generation (generate_proof)
  3. HealRecord dataclass and audit trail (heal_log)
  4. Tier-1 recovery from in-memory recovery_cache
  5. Tier-2 recovery from historical snapshot extents
  6. Multi-block corruption across multiple files
  7. Merkle root re-anchoring after heal
  8. Unrecoverable block reporting
  9. Post-heal Merkle scrub confirms HEALTHY status
 10. get_merkle_proof() exposed on AeroFileSystem

tests.name: test_scrub_all_files_returns_correct_structure
tests.doc: scrub_all_files() via scrub_all() returns a well-formed report dict.

tests.name: test_merkle_proof_generation_single_block
tests.doc: generate_proof() returns a valid path for a single-block file.

tests.name: test_merkle_proof_generation_multi_block
tests.doc: generate_proof() returns a non-empty sibling path for multi-block files.

tests.name: test_merkle_proof_invalid_index
tests.doc: generate_proof() returns valid=False for out-of-range indices.

tests.name: test_get_merkle_proof_on_filesystem
tests.doc: AeroFileSystem.get_merkle_proof() exposes proof API correctly.

tests.name: test_heal_log_is_empty_before_any_heal
tests.doc: No heal records exist before any healing operation.

tests.name: test_heal_log_records_one_entry_per_healed_block
tests.doc: heal_log accumulates exactly one HealRecord per corrupted block healed.

tests.name: test_heal_log_accumulates_across_multiple_heals
tests.doc: heal_log persists entries across successive self_heal_all() calls.

tests.name: test_tier1_cache_heals_corrupted_block
tests.doc: Single corrupted block is repaired from in-memory recovery cache.

tests.name: test_tier2_snapshot_path_exercised_when_cache_cleared
tests.doc:
When recovery_cache is cleared, self-healing falls back to the snapshot
extent search path. Reports the result (healed or unrecoverable) correctly.

tests.name: test_multi_file_multi_block_heal
tests.doc: Self-healing correctly repairs corruption spanning multiple files.

tests.name: test_merkle_root_re_anchored_after_heal
tests.doc:
After self-healing, the inode's merkle_root and leaf_hashes are updated
to reflect the clean repaired blocks, so subsequent scrubs pass cleanly.

tests.name: test_unrecoverable_block_reported_correctly
tests.doc:
A block with no cache entry and no matching snapshot data is reported
as unrecoverable, not silently ignored.

tests.name: test_post_heal_scrub_reflects_true_state
tests.doc: heal_all()'s built-in post-heal scrub always reflects true disk state.

tests.name: test_scrub_reports_orphan_device_corrupted_blocks
tests.doc:
Blocks flagged in dev.corrupted_blocks that are not owned by any active
inode are still captured in the scrub report as a 'Physical Storage Layer'
orphan entry.

tests/test_unrecoverable_safety.py.file_doc:
test_unrecoverable_safety.py
============================

Automated tests that prove AeroFS refuses to return corrupted data to user-space
when BOTH recovery sources (Tier-1 recovery cache and Tier-2 snapshots) are
missing or corrupted.

The tests confirm three precise behaviours:

  1. self_heal_all() reports DEGRADED status + block listed in unrecoverable_blocks
     when both tiers fail.
  2. read_file(filename) raises IntegrityError (subclass of IOError/EIO) instead of
     silently returning the corrupt bytes — this is the critical safety guarantee.
  3. read_file(filename, verify_integrity=False) returns raw bytes without raising,
     enabling forensic inspection without corrupting the guarantee for normal callers.

No third recovery source is added. The goal is safe failure, not hiding it.

tests.name: test_heal_reports_unrecoverable_block_when_cache_and_snapshots_both_missing
tests.doc:
Baseline: no cache, no snapshots → heal must report the block as unrecoverable
and post_heal_status must be DEGRADED.

tests.name: test_heal_reports_unrecoverable_when_snapshot_extent_store_also_missing
tests.doc:
Tier-2 snapshot extent store entries are also removed before corruption.
Ensure heal still reports DEGRADED and does not hallucinate a recovery.

tests.name: test_leaf_hash_not_overwritten_with_corrupt_value_on_failed_heal
tests.doc:
A failed heal MUST NOT update inode.leaf_hashes with the corrupt digest.
Doing so would cause future scrubs to report HEALTHY for a damaged file —
a catastrophic silent data corruption.

tests.name: test_read_raises_integrity_error_when_both_tiers_fail
tests.doc:
THE CORE SAFETY TEST.

After bit-rot with both cache and snapshots absent, calling read_file()
must raise IntegrityError (subclass of IOError) — not silently return
the corrupted bytes.

tests.name: test_read_raises_integrity_error_is_subclass_of_ioerror
tests.doc:
IntegrityError must be catchable as IOError so POSIX-aware callers
receive the standard errno=EIO signal.

tests.name: test_read_raises_only_for_corrupt_block_not_clean_file
tests.doc:
IntegrityError must be raised ONLY for the file whose block is corrupt.
A second, clean file must still be readable without error.

tests.name: test_read_heals_and_succeeds_when_cache_available
tests.doc:
When Tier-1 (cache) is available, read_file() must silently self-heal
on-demand and return the correct data — no exception raised.

tests.name: test_read_heals_and_succeeds_when_snapshot_available
tests.doc:
When Tier-2 (snapshot extent store) is available and cache is absent,
read_file() must silently self-heal and return the correct data.

tests.name: test_read_raises_when_all_snapshot_extents_are_wiped
tests.doc:
Snapshot exists but its extent store has been wiped (simulating snapshot
store loss). Both tiers fail → IntegrityError must be raised.

tests.name: test_forensic_mode_returns_raw_corrupt_bytes_without_raising
tests.doc:
read_file(filename, verify_integrity=False) must return raw bytes even
when the block is corrupt — no integrity check, no exception.
This is an opt-in forensic / debug escape-hatch.

tests.name: test_default_mode_still_raises_for_same_file
tests.doc:
Confirm the contrast: same scenario, default verify_integrity=True raises,
while verify_integrity=False does not.

tests.name: test_api_read_returns_500_when_both_tiers_fail
tests.doc:
The REST endpoint GET /api/files/read/{filename} must return HTTP 500
with an informative error message when read_file raises IntegrityError.

tests.class_doc:
Single-file, step-by-step demonstration of the core safety guarantee.
Mirrors precisely the scenario the OS project specification calls for.
tests.name: test_step_by_step_both_tiers_missing_raises_integrity_error
tests.doc:
CANONICAL SAFETY TEST — verbatim 4-step scenario.

Step 1: Write a file → record SHA-256 of original bytes.
Step 2: Corrupt one physical block.
Step 3: Remove both recovery sources (cache + all snapshot extents).
Step 4: Attempt to read the file.
Assert: IntegrityError is raised — corrupted bytes are never returned.

tests.class_doc:
Single-file, step-by-step demonstration of the core safety guarantee.
Mirrors precisely the scenario the OS project specification calls for.
tests.name: test_step_by_step_tier1_available_restores_original_bytes
tests.doc:
Same 4-step setup, but recovery cache is LEFT INTACT.
read_file must silently self-heal and return the original bytes.
SHA-256 of the returned data must match the original hash.

tests.class_doc:
Single-file, step-by-step demonstration of the core safety guarantee.
Mirrors precisely the scenario the OS project specification calls for.
tests.name: test_step_by_step_tier2_snapshot_available_restores_original_bytes
tests.doc:
Same setup, cache is wiped but a snapshot with a clean extent store exists.
read_file must silently self-heal via Tier-2 and return the original bytes.
SHA-256 of the returned data must match the original hash.

tests.class_doc:
Single-file, step-by-step demonstration of the core safety guarantee.
Mirrors precisely the scenario the OS project specification calls for.
tests.name: test_api_reports_500_not_200_with_corrupt_bytes
tests.doc:
Step-by-step scenario via the REST API.
When both tiers fail the server must return HTTP 500 — not HTTP 200
with the corrupt payload silently embedded in the JSON response.
